QUOTE: By default each field is really named `private_state`, `private_flags`, and so on. Code that writes `ssl->state` against the public header fails to compile, so the field is effectively private.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming members to `private_*` through name mangling, so access by the original name fails. It does not claim the layout is hidden, and the fields stay declared in the public struct.
